title: Guide - Grief and Comfort - Permission to grieve

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Grief and Comfort. <short pause> This practice is called Permission to Grieve. <short pause> I'm so sorry for what you have lost. <short pause> You don't have to be strong in here. <short pause> You don't have to be anything at all.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Let your body be as heavy as it is. <short pause> If tears come, let them come. <short pause> And if none come, that is all right too. <short pause> Grief can be loud, and it can be completely numb. <short pause> Both are grief... and both are welcome.

After a loss, people often mean to be kind, and they hand us reasons to stop crying. <short pause> At least it was quick. <short pause> At least you had those years. <short pause> Everything happens for a reason. <short pause> And we nod, and we thank them... and we learn to do our weeping in the car, or in the shower, where it won't trouble anyone.

There is a story in the Gospel of John about a family in Bethany. <short pause> Two sisters, Martha and Mary, and their brother Lazarus, whom Jesus loved. <short pause> Lazarus fell ill, and he died. <short pause> When Jesus arrived, each sister said the same thing to Him. <short pause> Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.

He didn't correct Mary. <short pause> He didn't tell her to dry her eyes. <short pause> He saw her weeping, and the friends weeping with her, and He was deeply troubled. <short pause> He asked where they had laid him, and they said... come and see. <short pause> And then we are given this, in John chapter eleven, verse thirty-five.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He knew what He was about to do. <short pause> He knew that in a little while, He would call His friend out of the grave. <short pause> And still, He cried. <short pause> Knowing the end of the story did not make the sorrow foolish. <short pause> So your hope of heaven doesn't have to cancel your tears. <short pause> You can believe with all your heart... and still stand at a grave and weep.

The people who were watching didn't say, look how weak His faith is. <short pause> They said, behold how He loved him. <short pause> That is what your grief is. <short pause> It is love, with the one it was given to out of reach. <short pause> There is nothing in it that you need to apologize for.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: So what have you not given yourself permission to feel? <short pause> Sadness, long after others expected it to pass? <short pause> Anger? Relief, after a long illness? <short pause> Laughter, that arrived at the wrong moment? <short pause> Or nothing... just a great, gray tiredness? <short pause> Choose whichever is truest, and let it have a place to sit.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: I'll say some words slowly, and you can receive the ones you need. <short pause> You may cry. <short pause> You may not cry. <short pause> You may miss them for as long as you live. <short pause> You may say their name out loud. <short pause> You may have a good hour, without feeling guilty. <short pause> You may have a terrible one, without explaining why. <short pause> You are allowed to grieve.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, who wept beside a grave, <short pause> thank You that I don't need to hide my sorrow from You. <short pause> You know the name I am carrying. <short pause> You know what went with them when they left. <short pause> Where I have scolded myself for hurting, teach me to be gentle. <short pause> And when I have no words, let my tears be the prayer. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, very slow blessing, resting between phrases
parts.text: There is nothing you need to finish before you go. <short pause> Take your grief with you, just as it is. <short pause> It is allowed to come along... <short pause> and so is the One who wept.
